crossroads.kicker: Story Crossroads • Tuesday, August 21, 2001, 9:48 AM — Norfolk Pathfinder Terminal
crossroads.title: Before the Walk-Up Ticket Line: Does Nolan Lock His Wheelchair Brakes or Stay Quiet?
crossroads.prompt: Inside the fluorescent-lit concourse of the Norfolk Pathfinder Terminal, twenty-six-year-old Tammy strides toward the walk-up plexiglass counter with an envelope of cash to buy two unreserved ninety-nine-dollar four-day bus tickets to Seattle—without calling Pathfinder forty-eight hours ahead for a hydraulic wheelchair lift. Twenty-three-year-old Nolan Lennox's Wednesday shift at the Emerald Creek Blue Tech is twenty-nine hours away, seventeen-year-old Gwen turns eighteen in October, and Grandpa Walter's heart is failing back in Chesapeake. Every option opens a complete, coequal story route that returns Nolan home to Studio 205 and Mallory Walsh before Vaeloria.

options.label: Lock Both Wheelchair Brakes & Break Up in Public
options.subtitle: Snap both steel wheel locks down in front of thirty concourse witnesses, refuse Tammy's last-ditch enticement in favor of yell-free peace with Gwen, and ride three CVTA buses safely home to Grandpa Walter's porch and your spotless Blue Tech schedule.

options.label: Freeze Under Conditioned Dread & Board the Seattle Pathfinder
options.subtitle: Stay quiet to avoid a concourse explosion and haul yourself up four steep aluminum coach steps on your matte-silver forearm crutches for a brutal ninety-six-hour coast-to-coast haul—while back at Blue Tech on Wednesday night, Shift Supervisor Mallory Walsh notices your first-ever missed shift.

crossroads.kicker: Story Crossroads • Wednesday, August 22, 2001, 8:05 PM — Emerald Creek Blue Tech
crossroads.title: Missed Shift Number One: Does Mallory Check on Nolan Tonight or Wait Until Friday?
crossroads.prompt: As Nolan's Pathfinder coach rolls west past St. Louis after his loose overhead wheelchair legrests crash down onto Tammy's head, eight-oh-five clicks onto the Emerald Creek Blue Tech breakroom timeclock—marking the first No-Call No-Show of Nolan's spotless two-year career. Quietly in love with Nolan yet bound both by respect for his relationship and by corporate HR's rule to wait until Friday's third missed shift, Computers Shift Supervisor Mallory Walsh stands beside her car four blocks from Grandpa Walter's house on Eden Way North. Both options return Nolan home to Studio 205 and Mallory before Vaeloria.

options.label: Drive Down Eden Way North Tonight & Intercept Pasco
options.subtitle: Break corporate HR's three-day waiting rule immediately on Wednesday night, uncover Tammy's cash Seattle route at Pinecrest Court with Gwen and Grandpa Walter on Thursday morning, and fly Meridian Airlines into Pasco Regional Airport to rescue Nolan minutes before Tammy leads him into the terminal restroom.

options.label: Respect Workplace Boundaries & Wait Until Friday's Third No-Show
options.subtitle: Honor corporate protocol and relationship guardrails until Friday evening's automatic third-strike termination—leaving feverish Nolan to endure the full haul to Seattle, Puget Sound General Hospital, grounded post-9/11 skies, and missing Gwen's eighteenth birthday while Grandpa Walter refuses to die until Gwen and Mallory bring Nolan home.

crossroads.kicker: Story Crossroads • Second Afternoon of the Twin Moons, The Sunken Milestone
crossroads.title: Three Gentle Roads Toward the Waystation: How Do Nolan and Gwen Travel?
crossroads.prompt: With both wheelchairs left behind in Studio 205 on Earth, barefoot twenty-four-year-old Nolan Lennox and his six-foot-one nineteen-year-old sister Gwen have learned why Vaeloria's sleeping Astrolabe answered Gwen's wish: only two inseparable, unhurried hearts can re-harmonize the twin rings and heal The Great Drift. Here at the Sunken Milestone, peddler Bramwell Kettle shows them three gentle 1980s-fantasy routes winding inward. Every option opens a complete, coequal story route.

options.label: The Glasswater Lantern-Barge Canal
options.subtitle: Step onto barge-master Maren's wide reed-and-cedar lantern boat—cuddling barefoot on cushioned planks with forearm crutches stowed safe beside the gunwale while Gwen's astronomy eye guides the barge through the misty stars of The Great Drift.

options.label: The Whisperwood Cushion-Moss Road
options.subtitle: Walk unhurriedly at your own forearm-crutch pace over three-inch velvet moss laid by the Slow-Footed Order, soaking bare feet in 98-degree mineral springs and curling up together in cozy stone shelters as your shared footsteps reawaken sleepy forest lanterns.

options.label: The Brass Counterweight Gondola Way
options.subtitle: Board the oak-and-brass water-balanced sky gondola rising smoothly into the Amber Crags past singing bronze wind-harps, helping the cliffside Star-Keepers recalibrate moon-rings knocked out of phase by The Great Drift.
